title: Epochs, Batches, and Learning Rates
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of epochs, batches, and learning rates in a PyTorch workflow.
Apply a small example of epochs, batches, and learning rates and interpret the output.
Identify a relevant limitation, debugging check, or reproducibility concern.

content.intro: Epochs, Batches, and Learning Rates: Training adjusts model parameters to reduce a loss. The usual loop performs a forward pass, calculates loss, backpropagates gradients, and asks an optimizer to update parameters. In this lesson, use a small example to make the inputs, outputs, and boundary conditions explicit.
content.why_it_matters: A correctly ordered training loop separates predictions from targets, tracks learning progress, and makes it possible to reproduce or resume an experiment. For this lesson, focus on batch size and the evidence you can collect from a controlled example.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Use model.train() for training, zero_grad(), forward/loss, backward(), and optimizer.step() in order; validate separately without parameter updates. The source topics for this lesson are: Batch size, Number of epochs, Learning-rate selection. Keep each topic connected to a checkable input/output behavior.

content_blocks.title: Read the example
content_blocks.text: Watch the loss tensor and parameter update around one optimizer step. Then run several steps and report actual observed loss instead of promising a fixed score. The example is a teaching-scale check, not evidence of a trained model score or a hardware-independent performance claim.

content_blocks.title: Guided PyTorch example
content_blocks.code:
import torch
pred = torch.tensor([[0.1, 0.9]])
target = torch.tensor([1])
print(torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(pred, target).ndim)

content.task: Try it yourself: Train a tiny linear model on synthetic data for a few steps, record loss, and add a separate evaluation loop. Record the observed result and one limitation; do not report an unrun training or performance result as measured.

troubleshooting.symptom: A tensor operation raises a shape, dtype, or device mismatch.
troubleshooting.check: Print .shape, .dtype, and .device for each input. Resolve the mismatch intentionally instead of changing dimensions blindly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The example fails because an optional package or accelerator is unavailable.
troubleshooting.check: Check the installed PyTorch/package versions and device availability. Use the official installation selector and run the CPU-compatible path where appropriate.

troubleshooting.symptom: The result differs across runs or machines.
troubleshooting.check: Fix the seed where useful, record versions and inputs, and document operations that remain nondeterministic or hardware dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on assumptions instead of inspecting the data or output.
common_mistakes.why: Many ML failures come from incorrect shapes, labels, preprocessing, or execution mode rather than a syntax error.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect representative inputs and add assertions for the expected shape, dtype, range, or behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing training-time behavior with inference-time behavior.
common_mistakes.why: Dropout, normalization, gradient tracking, and optimizer updates can change how a model behaves.
common_mistakes.fix: Do not call optimizer.step() before backward(), or evaluate validation data with the training-update path.

common_mistakes.problem: Using a current or experimental API without recording its version assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Hardware support and ecosystem APIs can change independently of the core package.
common_mistakes.fix: Pin compatible dependencies, record the environment, and test after upgrades.
